chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the pregnant female slave whom a man buys. He said, 'My father was asked about that and said, "A verse has made it permissible and another verse has made it forbidden." And I myself and my offspring are forbidding it." The man said, 'Then I hope to cease [from it] when you forbid yourself and your offspring.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a pregnant female slave according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the apparent textual ambiguity between the verse permitting concubinage (23:6) and the verse commanding emancipation upon request (24:33) by establishing a personal precedent (zahir al-zaman) for himself and his progeny. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of voluntary precaution (ihtiyat) in jurisprudence, where the Ahl al-Bayt voluntarily restrict permissible acts to elevate spiritual status and serve as a model for the community.
